description: See why a method that creates an unseeded Random instance inside its body is hard to unit-test deterministically.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import java.util.Random and define isHeads(), which creates new Random() on line 5 and draws double randomValue = rng.nextDouble() on line 9.
Set boolean result = false, change result to true if(randomValue > 0.5), and return result.
Call isHeads() twice in main and print each boolean return value.

steps.answer: new Random() on line 5 has no fixed seed. randomValue is generated inside isHeads() rather than passed as a parameter. It can be either above or below 0.5 on any call.
steps.question: Why can't a unit test predict whether isHeads() on line 20 will return true or false?

steps.description: Inspect randomValue and result inside the first call to isHeads() when randomValue > 0.5.

title: Testing Methods That Use Random Number Generators
